Name: test_no_ticket_gps_mismatch_clears_the_mismatch_radius
Description:
Uses the same distance check anomaly_detector.py itself runs, so
        this asserts the injected event will actually read as suspicious,
        not just that it's structurally valid.

        _random_road_coords() draws its jitter uniformly across the full
        attack_road_gps_jitter_deg box around a depot, which is wide enough
        that an UNSEEDED draw lands inside the 2km mismatch radius roughly
        1 time in 10 — a real, if narrow, edge case of the live demo
        trigger itself (an attacker could get GPS-unlucky and only trip
        the no_ticket_flag, not gps_mismatch_flag too), but not something
        this test should be flaky over. Seed=0 is pre-verified below to
        produce a draw that clears the threshold, so this test checks the
        mechanism deterministically rather than gambling on random draws.

Name: test_never_raises_even_on_total_failure
Description:
decide_for_asset must never propagate an exception — a fleet
        loop should never abort because one asset's LLM call kept failing.

Name: test_repair_cannot_bypass_vehicle_id_validation
Description:
A repaired-but-wrong-vehicle response must still be rejected by
        the same mismatch guard as a clean response would be — repair only
        fixes syntax, never relaxes the semantic checks after it.

Name: test_critical_flag_implies_sustained_flag
Description:
Critical temp threshold is higher than the safe threshold, so
        anything critical must also be above the safe threshold.

Name: test_fit_recovers_high_r_squared
Description:
The simulator's decay is genuinely exponential, so a good fit
        should be near-perfect — this is the core claim from the earlier
        'do we need a powerful model' discussion.

Name: test_attack_commands_have_no_ticket
Description:
This is the core ground-truth invariant: injected attacks must
        never have a matching maintenance ticket, or the whole premise
        of the detector (no-ticket = suspicious) breaks.

Name: test_no_false_positives_on_legitimate_commands
Description:
Legit commands (real ticket, depot GPS) should never be flagged
        suspicious — this is the assertion that would have caught the
        index-misalignment bug found during development.

Name: test_injected_command_is_flagged_by_the_real_anomaly_detector
Description:
End-to-end integration check: inject a live event, read it back
        exactly as risk_engine.py would, and confirm anomaly_detector.py
        actually flags it. This is the property the entire component
        exists to demonstrate — a passing unit test on the builder alone
        wouldn't catch a schema/column-name drift that broke detection.

Name: test_shifts_do_not_overlap_within_a_vehicle
Description:
The core correctness property: consecutive shift-assignment
        records for the same vehicle must be contiguous and non-
        overlapping, since a vehicle can't have two drivers at once.

Name: test_repeated_injection_accumulates_rather_than_overwrites
Description:
Each call generates a fresh uuid4 command_id, so back-to-back
        clicks of the demo button must both land — insert_command_batch's
        INSERT OR IGNORE dedup should never silently swallow the second one.

Name: test_telemetry_unique_constraint
Description:
(vehicle_id, cycle) must be unique — duplicate cycle for the same
        vehicle should be silently ignored, not inserted as a second row.

Name: test_every_scenario_validates_against_command_event_schema
Description:
If this fails, build_attack_commands' output shape has drifted
        from what ingestion/schemas.py — and therefore the rest of the
        pipeline — actually accepts.

Name: test_attacked_vehicle_risk_level_at_least_as_high_as_clean
Description:
The attacked vehicle's overall_risk_level must never rank below
        an otherwise-identical clean vehicle's — security signal should
        only ever push risk up, never down.

Name: test_no_decay_curve_returns_none_rul
Description: Flat capacity (no measurable decay) must not fabricate an RUL number.

Name: test_foreign_key_integrity
Description:
Every driver_id in vehicle_assignments must reference a real
        driver — catches a schema/generator drift the same way
        test_ingestion.py's test_foreign_key_integrity does for
        commands -> maintenance_tickets.

Name: test_charge_stress_score_formula
Description:
Score = 0.4*fast_freq + 0.4*min(dod,100) + 0.2*high_dod_freq — verify
        the documented weighting is actually what's implemented.

Name: test_rul_decreases_as_capacity_approaches_eol
Description:
Two synthetic curves with identical decay rate but different
        current position — the one closer to EOL must report lower RUL.

Name: test_all_true_thermal_events_are_flagged
Description:
Full recall: every simulator-injected thermal event must be caught.
        (Precision is expected to be looser — the detector flags any reading
        above threshold, which is broader but not wrong; see project notes.)

Name: test_wrong_vehicle_id_from_model_never_gets_misattributed
Description:
If the model ever echoes back a different asset's ID (e.g.
        confused by the few-shot example, which itself references
        'EVR-0042'), decide_for_asset must NOT silently attribute that
        action to the asset we actually asked about — it should exhaust
        retries and fall back to an explicit review-needed decision
        instead of mislabeling which vehicle an action belongs to.

Name: test_unknown_scenario_falls_back_to_single_gps_mismatch_command
Description:
build_attack_commands treats anything outside the known scenario
        keys as the default single-command case rather than raising — a
        stray/renamed scenario string should degrade safely, not crash the
        Streamlit callback mid-demo.

Name: test_extra_field_rejected
Description:
model_config = {'extra': 'forbid'} should reject unknown fields —
        catches silent data-shape drift between simulator and schema.

Name: test_fallback_is_itself_a_valid_shape
Description:
The fallback must pass the exact same validator real responses
        do, since actions.execute_decision() doesn't know it's a fallback.

Name: test_each_decision_matches_the_asset_it_was_built_for
Description:
Regression guard: catches any accidental index/order mismatch
        between the risk profile rows and the decisions returned for them
        (the same class of bug test_anomaly_detector.py guards against).

Name: test_all_attacks_have_at_least_one_signal
Description:
Every injected attack must be caught by at least one signal —
        primarily no_ticket_flag, since attacks are always ticketless.

Name: test_unticketed_commands_match_attack_count
Description:
The core invariant: DB-side 'no ticket' must equal simulator-side
        'is_attack' count, or the security-anomaly precondition breaks.

Name: test_genuinely_unrepairable_input_still_raises
Description:
Repair must not turn 'nonsense' into a false-positive parse that
        silently produces a wrong/empty decision — plain prose should still
        fail loudly rather than be coerced into something misleading.

Name: test_assignment_shift_end_is_optional
Description:
The simulator always produces a concrete shift_end, but real
        (live) ingestion should be able to accept an in-progress shift
        without one yet.

Name: test_unescaped_quote_in_rationale_is_repaired
Description:
The exact failure shape that motivated adding repair at all:
        json.loads alone raises here; _validate_and_normalize must recover
        it via _attempt_json_repair rather than falling back.

Name: test_foreign_key_integrity
Description: Every non-null ticket_id in commands must reference a real ticket.

Name: test_timestamps_are_anchored_to_now_not_a_simulated_past
Description:
The whole reason this component exists separately from
        simulator/attack_injector.py: the injected event must be 'live',
        not drawn from a historical vehicle_time_bounds window.

Name: test_capacity_trends_downward
Description: Capacity should generally fade over cycles, not trend up.

Name: test_at_least_one_attack_injected
Description:
With attack_injection_rate_pct > 0 and a non-trivial fleet size,
        we expect at least one attack in the stream.
